title: intent
description: The structured output the LLM must return per message. Validated in n8n against THIS file. A failure is always visible, but the class depends on WHICH failure (see .claude/rules/handoff.md): the model not answering at all (bad stop_reason, unparseable JSON, non-object) hands off and locks; a well-formed answer that violates THIS schema is USUALLY extraction-transient — owner-alerted, kept off every write path, no stage write — and then escalates on a SECOND consecutive one. THREE exceptions, written here because the sentence was false at its own use site (Codex round 4): (1) if the intent is 'handoff' it locks on turn one like any explicit handoff; (2) if a cancel/reschedule confirmation is pending it locks on turn one, because a pending booking must not hang on a classification we distrust; (3) the three non-schema failures (bad stop_reason, unparseable JSON, non-object) never enter this class at all.

intent.description: Allow-list only — no other action exists.

dateExpr.description: The customer's OWN wording for the DAY, copied VERBATIM and lowercased — including an absolute date they typed themselves ("friday", "this friday", "friday morning", "tomorrow", "2026-09-11"). NEVER a date YOU computed: the engine resolves the day deterministically in the shop timezone, and an ISO date here is accepted only when that exact string appears in the customer's own message. null ONLY when the customer named no day at all. REQUIRED — a missing key is a contract violation, because the engine cannot distinguish an absent field from a deliberate null, and that ambiguity is what let the model bypass the guard entirely (Codex finding 3).

faqTopic.description: For answer_faq only — the FAQ category. Combined with serviceId for price questions.

reply.description: Optional draft reply text; deterministic templates from config are preferred.
